```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Lee 2020 builds a Level A in vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC) for
subcutaneous leuprolide acetate PLGA microspheres in rats. One structural
model -- a release compartment fed by a non-capsuled burst fraction and by a
diffusive and an erosive transit chain, absorbed into a one-compartment
disposition model -- is fitted separately to six formulations:

* the marketed Lucrin depot microspheres, fitted to the observed plasma
  leuprolide profile of five rats, and
* five electrosprayed microsphere formulations (OL1-OL5, differing in the
  RG502:RG502H PLGA ratio), fitted to the in vivo release profile the IVIVC
  predicts from each formulation's in vitro release test.

The disposition parameters (ka, CL/F, Vd/F) are the same in all six and are
carried from the authors' earlier solution study (Lee 2018, also in this
package as `Lee_2018_leuprolide_sc_rat`). The six independent fits give six
model files.

```{r models}
forms <- c("lucrin", "ol1", "ol2", "ol3", "ol4", "ol5")
form_labels <- c(
  lucrin = "Lucrin depot",
  ol1 = "OL1", ol2 = "OL2", ol3 = "OL3", ol4 = "OL4", ol5 = "OL5"
)
model_names <- sprintf("Lee_2020_leuprolide_%s_rat", forms)
names(model_names) <- forms
uis <- lapply(model_names, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))

tibble::tibble(
  Model = unname(model_names),
  Formulation = c(
    "Lucrin depot (reference product; fitted to plasma PK)",
    "OL1, RG502:RG502H 50:50 (fitted to IVIVC-predicted release)",
    "OL2, RG502:RG502H 75:25 (fitted to IVIVC-predicted release)",
    "OL3, RG502:RG502H 100:0 (fitted to IVIVC-predicted release)",
    "OL4, RG502:RG502H 25:75 (fitted to IVIVC-predicted release)",
    "OL5, RG502:RG502H 0:100 (fitted to IVIVC-predicted release; validated in vivo)"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The six models this paper contributes.")
```

* Citation: `r uis[[1]]$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics12010036>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7022573/>

The paper also reports plasma testosterone after Lucrin depot and OL5
(Figure 7) but fits no PD model to it; the testosterone feedback model for the
same rats and products is the one in Lee 2018.

# Population

Fifteen male Wistar rats were used (Methods 2.3); ten of them formed the PK/PD
study, five receiving Lucrin depot and five OL5, each as a single
subcutaneous dose equivalent to 0.1 mg/kg leuprolide acetate (Methods
2.10.1). Body weight is not reported. Every row of Table 3 gives
CL/F x AUCinf = 25,000 ng (for example 475.97 mL/h x 52.52 h*ng/mL for OL5),
so the dose used throughout this vignette is 25,000 ng per rat. OL1-OL4 were
never given to animals: their release parameters come from the in vitro
release test (Figure 4, n = 3) time-scaled to in vivo.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value(s) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: NS, DS1..DSn, ES1..ESn, central | -- | Methods 2.9.1, Equation 1, Figure 2 |
| Initial NS, DS1, ES1 = dose x E1, E2, E3 | -- | Methods 2.9.1 (text below Equation 1) |
| ka | 16.67 1/h | Methods 2.9.1 (from Lee 2018 solution group) |
| CL/F | 514.46 mL/h | Methods 2.9.1 |
| Vd/F | 487.40 mL | Methods 2.9.1 |
| E1, E2, E3 | per formulation | Table 2; Results 3.5.1 (Lucrin), 3.5.2 (OL1-OL5) |
| Number of transit (DS), (ES) | per formulation | Table 2 |
| ktr-d, ktr-e | per formulation | Table 2 |
| Levy-plot Hill correlation a, b, c | 696.87, 1.75, 25.91 | Equation 3, Results 3.5.1 |
| Cumulative-release times | 20-70 % | Table 1 |
| Predicted Cmax / AUCinf | per formulation | Table 3 |
| Residual error, between-animal variability | not reported | -- |

```{r params}
param_tab <- lapply(forms, function(f) {
  ini <- uis[[f]]$theta
  e1 <- plogis(ini[["logitfrel"]])
  e2 <- (1 - e1) * plogis(ini[["logitfrel2"]])
  states <- uis[[f]]$state
  tibble::tibble(
    Formulation = form_labels[[f]],
    E1 = round(e1, 3),
    E2 = round(e2, 3),
    E3 = round(1 - e1 - e2, 3),
    `DS stages` = sum(grepl("^transit_fast", states)),
    `ES stages` = sum(grepl("^transit_slow", states)),
    `ktr-d (1/h)` = signif(exp(ini[["lktr_fast"]]), 3),
    `ktr-e (1/h)` = signif(exp(ini[["lktr_slow"]]), 3)
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
knitr::kable(param_tab, caption = "Release parameters as packaged (compare Table 2).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Transit-stage counts.** Table 2 prints non-integer numbers of transit
  compartments for OL1-OL5 (for example 2.759 for the OL3 diffusive chain),
  while Equation 1 writes each chain as discrete compartments. The packaged
  models round each count to the nearest integer (DS: 2 stages, 3 for OL3;
  ES: 2 stages). The check below shows that this reading reproduces the
  curves of Figure 6A and that the continuous (gamma-distributed) reading does
  not. Lucrin depot's counts (1 and 2) are printed as integers.
* **Erosive chain rate constant.** Equation 1 as printed writes `ktr-d` for the
  transfers inside the ES chain and `ktr-e` for its outflow into NS, which
  would not conserve mass. The text (Methods 2.9.1: "ktr-e is the erosive
  release constant from ES to NS") and Figure 2 both assign ktr-e to the ES
  section, so the packaged models run the whole ES chain at ktr-e.
* **Dose.** 25,000 ng per rat, back-calculated from Table 3 as described
  under Population.
* **Disposition parameters held at the Lee 2018 values.** They are encoded as
  `fixed()` because this paper does not estimate them.
* **No variability.** The fits are to mean profiles in Berkeley Madonna; no
  residual error or between-animal variability is reported, so the
  proportional residual SD is `fixed(0)` and there are no random effects.
* **Levy-plot correlation.** Equation 3 maps in vivo to in vitro release time.
  It is how the OL1-OL5 release parameters were obtained, not part of the
  ODE model, so it is reproduced below as a check rather than packaged.
* **Single dose.** The release sections are loaded by three simultaneous dose
  records (amounts split by `f()`), so repeated doses superpose correctly, but
  the paper studied single doses only.

# Simulation

All six models are deterministic. Each formulation receives 25,000 ng split
by `f()` across the release compartment and the first compartment of each
transit chain.

```{r simulate}
dose <- 25000
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, 24, by = 0.1), seq(24, 336, by = 0.5))))

make_events <- function(cmts, amt, times) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, cmt = cmts[1])
  for (cc in cmts[-1]) ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = amt, cmt = cc)
  rxode2::et(ev, times, cmt = "central")
}
ev <- make_events(c("depot", "transit_fast1", "transit_slow1"), dose, grid)

sim <- lapply(forms, function(f) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(uis[[f]], ev, atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10)) |>
    dplyr::select(time, Cc, dplyr::starts_with("transit")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(formulation = form_labels[[f]], .before = 1)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(formulation = factor(formulation, levels = form_labels))
```

```{r fig6a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6A of Lee 2020: Lucrin depot (packaged fit) and the IVIVC-predicted profiles of OL1-OL5."}
ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim, Cc > 1e-5), aes(time, Cc, colour = formulation)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-5, 100)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 336, by = 56)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma leuprolide (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Check 1 - Figure 6A and the transit-stage counts

The maintainers digitised the OL1-OL5 curves of Figure 6A (published
722 x 379 px raster; log axis 1e-5 to 1e2) at the times below. The packaged
(rounded) models are compared against those values. The continuous reading
is computed alongside it with the same parameters, replacing each chain by its
gamma-distributed outflow `A0 * ktr * (ktr t)^(n-1) * exp(-ktr t) / Gamma(n)`.

```{r fig6a-digitised}
digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~formulation, ~time, ~fig6a,
  "OL1", 8, 0.30, "OL1", 12, 0.39, "OL1", 20, 0.48, "OL1", 112, 0.031,
  "OL1", 280, 0.0031, "OL1", 322, 0.0034,
  "OL2", 8, 0.12, "OL2", 10, 0.14, "OL2", 20, 0.22, "OL2", 56, 0.25,
  "OL2", 112, 0.12, "OL2", 280, 0.0042,
  "OL3", 8, 0.029, "OL3", 10, 0.024, "OL3", 12, 0.028, "OL3", 16, 0.039,
  "OL3", 20, 0.054, "OL3", 28, 0.074, "OL3", 40, 0.091, "OL3", 56, 0.098,
  "OL3", 112, 0.074, "OL3", 280, 0.026, "OL3", 322, 0.020,
  "OL4", 4, 0.46, "OL4", 6, 0.37, "OL4", 12, 0.56, "OL4", 16, 0.63,
  "OL4", 20, 0.68, "OL4", 28, 0.66, "OL4", 40, 0.55, "OL4", 56, 0.36,
  "OL4", 70, 0.24, "OL4", 168, 0.0061, "OL4", 224, 0.00057, "OL4", 280, 5.3e-5,
  "OL5", 4, 0.84, "OL5", 8, 1.2, "OL5", 16, 1.3, "OL5", 20, 1.1, "OL5", 56, 0.14
)

# Continuous-count reading: the same release parameters, each chain replaced by
# its closed-form gamma outflow with the printed non-integer stage count.
gamma_mod <- rxode2::rxode2({
  rin_d <- E2 * dose * exp(log(kd) + (nd - 1) * log(kd * t + 1e-300) - kd * t - lgamma(nd))
  rin_e <- E3 * dose * exp(log(ke) + (ne - 1) * log(ke * t + 1e-300) - ke * t - lgamma(ne))
  d/dt(depot) <- rin_d + rin_e - ka * depot
  d/dt(central) <- ka * depot - cl / vc * central
  depot(0) <- E1 * dose
  Cc <- central / vc
})
table2_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  formulation = c("OL1", "OL2", "OL3", "OL4", "OL5"),
  nd = c(2.478, 2.364, 2.759, 2.020, 2.002),
  ne = c(2.210, 2.000, 2.195, 2.068, 2)
)
gamma_pred <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(table2_counts)), function(i) {
  f <- tolower(table2_counts$formulation[i])
  th <- uis[[f]]$theta
  e1 <- plogis(th[["logitfrel"]])
  e2 <- (1 - e1) * plogis(th[["logitfrel2"]])
  p <- c(
    E2 = e2, E3 = 1 - e1 - e2, E1 = e1, dose = dose,
    kd = exp(th[["lktr_fast"]]), ke = exp(th[["lktr_slow"]]),
    nd = table2_counts$nd[i], ne = table2_counts$ne[i],
    ka = exp(th[["lka"]]), cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]), vc = exp(th[["lvc"]])
  )
  times <- digitised$time[digitised$formulation == table2_counts$formulation[i]]
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(gamma_mod, p, rxode2::et(times), atol = 1e-14, rtol = 1e-10))
  tibble::tibble(formulation = table2_counts$formulation[i], time = s$time, gamma = s$Cc)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

fig6a_cmp <- digitised |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim |>
      dplyr::mutate(formulation = as.character(formulation)) |>
      dplyr::select(formulation, time, packaged = Cc),
    by = c("formulation", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(gamma_pred, by = c("formulation", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_packaged = 100 * (packaged - fig6a) / fig6a,
    pct_gamma = 100 * (gamma - fig6a) / fig6a
  )

fig6a_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(fig6a, packaged, gamma), \(x) signif(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(pct_packaged, pct_gamma), \(x) round(x))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Formulation = formulation, `Time (h)` = time, `Figure 6A (ng/mL)` = fig6a,
    `Packaged, rounded counts (ng/mL)` = packaged,
    `Continuous counts (ng/mL)` = gamma,
    `Rounded vs figure (%)` = pct_packaged, `Continuous vs figure (%)` = pct_gamma
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Concentrations against the digitised Figure 6A.")

fig6a_summary <- fig6a_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(formulation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_abs_pct_rounded = median(abs(pct_packaged)),
    median_abs_pct_continuous = median(abs(pct_gamma))
  )
knitr::kable(fig6a_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Median absolute deviation from Figure 6A by reading.")
```

The rounded counts follow the figure to within the reading precision of a
small raster (median deviation 2-5 % per formulation). The continuous reading
misses OL1 and OL2 by a median of 35-45 %, putting the diffusive peak too late
and too low, and underpredicts the OL3 plateau at 56-112 h by 12-14 %; these
are the three formulations whose printed counts are furthest from an integer.
OL4 and OL5 have counts within 0.07 of 2, so the two readings coincide there.

```{r fig6a-assert}
stopifnot(
  # Every formulation tracks the digitised figure; digitising a 379-px log axis
  # carries roughly +/-10 % per point, so the bound sits on the median.
  all(fig6a_summary$median_abs_pct_rounded < 10),
  # The continuous reading is clearly worse for the three non-integer cases.
  all(
    fig6a_summary$median_abs_pct_continuous[fig6a_summary$formulation %in% c("OL1", "OL2", "OL3")] >
      2 * fig6a_summary$median_abs_pct_rounded[fig6a_summary$formulation %in% c("OL1", "OL2", "OL3")]
  )
)
```

## Check 2 - Table 1 in vivo release times (Lucrin depot)

The predicted in vivo release is the fraction of the dose that has left the
microsphere sections and reached the release compartment: E1 at time zero
plus the cumulative outflow of both transit chains, i.e.
`1 - (amount still in the transit chains) / dose`. Table 1 lists the in vivo
times at which the Lucrin depot fit reaches 20-70 % release.

```{r table1}
lucrin <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(formulation == "Lucrin depot") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    released = 1 - (rowSums(dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("transit")), na.rm = TRUE)) / dose
  )

table1 <- tibble::tibble(
  pct = c(20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70),
  in_vivo_paper = c(0.7, 4.4, 9.6, 18.6, 46.2, 128.5),
  in_vitro_paper = c(3.4, 20.4, 88.2, 270.9, 497.3, 663.0)
)
table1$in_vivo_model <- approx(lucrin$released, lucrin$time, table1$pct / 100, ties = "ordered")$y

# Equation 3: in vitro time = a * t^b / (c^b + t^b)
levy <- function(t, a = 696.87, b = 1.75, c = 25.91) a * t^b / (c^b + t^b)
table1$in_vitro_eq3 <- levy(table1$in_vivo_paper)

table1 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(in_vivo_model, in_vitro_eq3), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `Cumulative release (%)` = pct,
    `In vivo time, Table 1 (h)` = in_vivo_paper,
    `In vivo time, packaged model (h)` = in_vivo_model,
    `In vitro time, Table 1 (h)` = in_vitro_paper,
    `In vitro time, Equation 3 (h)` = in_vitro_eq3
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 1 against the packaged Lucrin depot model and Equation 3.")
```

```{r fig5a, fig.cap = "Predicted in vivo cumulative release of Lucrin depot (cf. the solid line of Figure 5A), with the Table 1 in vivo times as points."}
ggplot(dplyr::filter(lucrin, time <= 336), aes(time, 100 * released)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = table1, aes(in_vivo_paper, pct), colour = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 336, by = 56)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cumulative in vivo release (%)") +
  theme_bw()
```

From 30 % upwards the packaged model reaches each release level within 10 %
of the Table 1 time, consistently a little early (for example 18.1 h against
18.6 h for 50 % and 126 h against 128.5 h for 70 %). The 20 % row is the
exception: the model releases E1 = 19 % at time zero and reaches 20 % at
0.3 h, against 0.7 h in Table 1, a difference of a fraction of an hour that
the printed E1 and ktr-d (rounded to two significant figures) cannot resolve.
Equation 3 reproduces the Table 1 in vitro times to within 8 % at 50 % release
and above; at 20-40 % it is off by 18-63 %, which an R-square of 0.997 on an
untransformed time scale dominated by the late points still allows.

```{r table1-assert}
stopifnot(
  all(abs(table1$in_vivo_model[-1] - table1$in_vivo_paper[-1]) / table1$in_vivo_paper[-1] < 0.1)
)
```

## Check 3 - PKNCA against Table 3

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(formulation)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, formulation, time, Cc)

# The solve grid starts at time 0, so every profile already has its time-zero
# row; the defensive row is discarded by distinct().
nca_in <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_in,
  nca_in |> dplyr::distinct(id, formulation) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, formulation, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | formulation + id)
dose_df <- nca_in |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, formulation) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | formulation + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tibble(
  formulation = unname(form_labels),
  cmax = c(8.53, 7.46, 12.93, 26.29, 9.05, 4.01),
  aucinf.obs = c(52.51, 36.82, 46.10, 54.21, 51.20, 52.52)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "formulation",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Table 3 NCA (Lucrin depot: observed; OL1-OL5: IVIVC-predicted). * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

Cmax agrees with Table 3 for every formulation; it is set by the burst
fraction E1, ka and the disposition parameters, and the simulated OL1-OL5
values run consistently 1.2-1.3 % below the table. The Lucrin depot entries
of Table 3 are observed NCA values, not model predictions, so its row (3 %
below) compares the fit against the data.

AUCinf from the simulation is 5-10 % below Table 3 for Lucrin depot and
OL2-OL5. Four Table 3 AUCinf values (Lucrin depot, OL3, OL4, OL5) exceed
dose / CL = 25,000 / 514.46 = 48.6 h*ng/mL, the total exposure of the whole
dose in this model, so they include area extrapolated beyond 14 days from a
slowly declining (or still-rising) tail; the extrapolation method and window
are not stated, and the simulated AUCinf depends on the same choice (the
Lucrin depot value here, 49.6 h*ng/mL, also exceeds 48.6 for that reason).
For OL1 the erosive chain is still raising the concentration at 336 h
(Figure 6A), so PKNCA finds no terminal phase and reports no AUCinf; its
AUC0-336 is 34.9 h*ng/mL against the Table 3 AUCinf of 36.82.

The observed OL5 values of the validation study (Cmax 4.14 ng/mL, AUCinf
56.95 h*ng/mL; Results 3.5.3) are 4 % and 14 % above the simulation.

```{r pknca-assert}
sim_vals <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(formulation, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(formulation = as.character(formulation)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published, by = "formulation", suffix = c("_sim", "_paper"))
stopifnot(
  # The two sides use the same deterministic parameters, so Cmax is tight.
  all(abs(sim_vals$cmax_sim / sim_vals$cmax_paper - 1) < 0.05),
  # The observed part of every profile carries no more than the whole dose.
  all(sim_vals$auclast <= dose / exp(uis[[1]]$theta[["lcl"]])),
  # OL1 has no terminal phase by 336 h; the others extrapolate.
  is.na(sim_vals$aucinf.obs_sim[sim_vals$formulation == "OL1"]),
  all(abs(sim_vals$aucinf.obs_sim / sim_vals$aucinf.obs_paper - 1) < 0.15, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```
